content.overview: Plausible Analytics is a lightweight, privacy-friendly web analytics tool that serves as an ethical alternative to Google Analytics. The script weighs under 1 KB — 45x smaller than Google Analytics — resulting in faster page loads. Plausible is fully GDPR, CCPA, and PECR compliant out of the box: it doesn't use cookies, doesn't collect personal data, and doesn't track users across sites. The dashboard is clean and intuitive, showing essential metrics: unique visitors, page views, bounce rate, visit duration, top pages, referral sources, countries, devices, and custom events. All data is aggregated — no individual user profiling. The self-hosted version is free and open-source (AGPL), while the cloud version starts at €9/month. For site owners who value user privacy and want simple, actionable analytics without the bloat of Google Analytics, Plausible is the clear winner.
pros: Under 1 KB script — 45x smaller than Google Analytics, faster page loads
GDPR, CCPA, PECR compliant by default: no cookies, no personal data collection
Clean dashboard with only essential metrics — no analysis paralysis
Self-hosted version is free and open-source (AGPL-3.0)
Custom event tracking for goals, clicks, and conversions
cons: Limited compared to GA4: no funnel analysis, no audience segmentation, no attribution modeling
Requires running a server for self-hosted; cloud version starts at €9/month
bestUseCases: Privacy-focused websites that want analytics without tracking users
Simple traffic monitoring for blogs, portfolios, and small business sites
